Correction Feedback

Dr B Townsend
The Emergency Department
Newtown Children’s Hospital

10/04/2010

Re: Miss Emma Johnson, aged 11 years

Dear Dr Townsend,

I am writing to refer Emma, who is suffering from an acute attack of severe asthma, for your urgent
assessment. [Avoid one-sentence paragraph]

Today, Emma presented with progressive shortness of breath and wheezing which have been
lasting for the previous 48 hours. On examination, dyspnoea and the use of accessory muscles of
respiration were noted. Chest auscultation revealed a wide-spread wheeze with no focal signs and
the peak expiratory flow rate was 140 L/min. Besides that, she also had a fever, loss of appetite, a
runny nose and a red throat, indicating the presence of an upper respiratory tract infection as a
precipitating factor to this asthma attack. Ventolin nebulizer was tried; however, the response was
minimal.

Emma is a known asthmatic patient with a positive family history related to her older sister and her
mother. Emma’s symptoms, including cough at night and after exercise and wheezes, started in           Commented [t1]: Her
November of 2009 after a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Over the following months, her
condition partially improved after the introduction of inhaled salbutamol, two puffs three times a
day, and her asthma was eventually well-controlled after adding an inhaled corticosteroid,
Becotide, two puffs three times per day to her treatment.

Emma is a known asthmatic patient with a positive family history related to her older sister and
her mother. Kindly note that she has no known allergies.

Regarding Emma’s current exacerbation, I believe she needs your urgent evaluation and                  Commented [ms2]: avoid verbs of personal judgement
management. Kindly, note that she has no known allergies.                                              Commented [ms3]: her condition


Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely
Doctor
